messages:
sara: FYI I'm opening a war-room — multiple customers reporting intermittent 5xx/504s hitting hosted /v1/generate since ~08:30 UTC. Support ticket RN-4523, customers A and B impacted. Observed spike in 5xx rate from api-gateway.
support-bot: Alert: hosted-api: error-rate 5xx > 5% for 3m on route /v1/generate (link to grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123)

mike: Can someone paste a couple of request_ids and any backend traces? need to see where it's failing (gateway vs runtime).

anna: Request IDs: req_9a1f, req_d4c2. From traces it looks like auth-proxy is timing out validating customer tokens — blocking upstream calls. Example from auth-proxy log:
```
[2026-02-28T08:31:12Z] req=req_9a1f auth-proxy: validating token -> POST billing-service/validate 504 (context deadline exceeded)
[2026-02-28T08:31:13Z] req=req_9a1f auth-proxy: error validating token: timeout
```

raj: I'm seeing elevated latency on billing-service -> KMS for signature checks. KMS requests spiking and hitting per-region concurrency limits. billing logs:
```
2026-02-28T08:30:58Z billing-service: kms.SignData latency 1200ms (concurrency 48/50)
2026-02-28T08:30:59Z billing-service: kms.SignData error: RateLimitExceeded
```

jen: So chain is: api-gateway -> auth-proxy (sync call to billing-service) -> billing-service -> KMS. If KMS is slow, auth-proxy blocks and gateway returns 504/502. Makes sense.

mike: Immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase auth-proxy timeout to allow more headroom, 2) fail-fast in auth-proxy for billing checks and serve cached token results for 60s, 3) route traffic to fallback region where KMS quotas are OK. Any objections to doing (2) as a hotfix?

ops-oncall: We should prefer fail-fast + cache to avoid head-of-line blocking. Increasing timeout will just let requests pile. Recommend short TTL cache for token validation and a circuit breaker to return 401/403 if billing validation unavailable for too long.

sara: Agreed. Raj / Jen can you scope quick patch for auth-proxy: add in-memory token-result cache + fail-fast path toggled by feature flag? We'll roll to canary and monitor 5xx rate.

raj: On it. I'll open a PR with a feature-flagged change and include a metrics counter. ETA 30m for PR + canary rollout. Will include a knob to bypass billing KMS call for internal/test keys.

anna: Support: messaging to customers (A,B) prepared: offer credits for downtime and explain we have a mitigation rolling now. I'll send updates once canary is green.

mike: Repro steps for SRE: to reproduce locally (short):
```
# simulate timeout path
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
# tail auth-proxy logs: kubectl -n platform logs -l app=auth-proxy | grep req_9a1f
```

jen: Long-term action items: (A) add async validation path so inference runtime doesn't block on billing/KMS, (B) request increased KMS quotas for eu-west, (C) add SLOs/alerting for downstream KMS latency and circuit-breaker metrics.

sara: Action items and owners:
- raj: PR for auth-proxy fail-fast + cache, feature flag (due: today EOD)
- mike: roll canary + monitor 5xx (start now)
- anna: customer comms + credits (notify by EOD)
- jen: KMS quota request + design async validation (due: 3/7)
- ops-oncall: add grafana panels and alert for kms latency (due: 3/2)

sara: Thanks all. I'll post a follow-up when canary shows 5xx back to baseline :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: Noted, attaching runbook snippet for next oncall: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/auth-proxy-5xx
sara: Closing loop: canary rolled at 08:55, initial results look good — 5xx down from 7.2% -> 0.8% in 10m window. Keeping channel open for postmortem notes and follow-ups.
